Counsel for Applicant :- Shree Prakash Giri Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 743 of 2021, under sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 472 and 120-B I.P.C., 66-C and 66-D IT Act, Police Station Jagdishpura, District Agra.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in this case applicant is a lady and was working as call agent on mobile telephone on the company said to be operated by co-accused Prem Singh, Saurabh Sharma, Deepak Kumar and Jeetu Singh.
It is further submitted that the applicant was not arrested from the spot with other co-accused persons but on the statement made by co-accused persons her name was mentioned in the F.I.R.

Further submitted that the preset applicant was not involved in the alleged fraudulent transaction done by the aforesaid company Afreen vs State Of U.P.And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54892864/
1 named as Andromeda Sales and Distribution Private Limited.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that investigation is going on and applicant is ready to make co-operation with the investigation but the applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation, so requested for anticipatory bail.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.

On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and his antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.

opennyai_summary.facts: This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 743 of 2021, under sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 472 and 120-B I.P.C., 66-C and 66-D IT Act, Police Station Jagdishpura, District Agra.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Further submitted that the preset applicant was not involved in the alleged fraudulent transaction done by the aforesaid company Afreen vs State Of U.P.And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54892864/
1 named as Andromeda Sales and Distribution Private Limited.
It is further submitted that investigation is going on and applicant is ready to make co-operation with the investigation but the applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation, so requested for anticipatory bail.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.
opennyai_summary.decision:
On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and his antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
In the event of arrest of the applicant- Afreen, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.
25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make herself available for interrogation by a police office as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if she has passport, the same shall be deposited by her before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
